CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 20, audited at commit 5e10fd8 (HEAD of the main checkout). Sprint
file re-read fresh immediately before this verdict, including the 23 Aug re-scope that
removed frames 1 and 2. Three files, 257 insertions.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. One required fix, and it is the one requirement in this
sprint that is not a matter of taste.

REQUIRED FIX -- R4's 44px touch target is not established, and my arithmetic says it
falls just short.

At the breakpoint, .castButton becomes:

    .castButton { padding: 14px; flex: 1; text-align: center; }

inheriting font-size: 10.5px, a 1px border, no line-height, and no min-height. So the
rendered height is 14*2 + 1*2 + one normal line box = 30px + line box. To clear 44px
the line box must be at least 14px, which at 10.5px means a normal line-height of at
least 1.33. IBM Plex Mono's normal metric is around 1.3, which puts this at roughly
43.7px -- under an explicit accessibility floor by a fraction of a pixel.

I could not settle it. There is no font parser available here (no fonttools, no
brotli, nothing in node_modules), the .woff2 files are compressed, and GroundTruth has
no browser. So I am not claiming this is definitely broken. I am claiming something
worse for a floor: **it cannot be verified by reading, and the arithmetic points the
wrong way.**

The requirement calls this "an accessibility floor, not a style preference", and the
criterion says "interactive targets meet 44px at 390px". A floor that depends on an
unmeasured font metric landing on the right side of a 0.3px margin is not a floor.
Adding `min-height: 44px` to that rule makes it true by construction and makes it
checkable by reading the stylesheet, which is the only way any gate in this process
can ever confirm it. One line.

Worth noting where the requirement's own 17px figure comes from, because it is not
wrong so much as inherited: the handoff states "17px inputs, 17px button padding --
every target clears 44px" at line 82, inside **Frame 1 -- /chart, entry**, which this
sprint removed from scope. So the specific number was written for frames this sprint
no longer builds. The floor still applies to frames 3 and 4; the number does not
automatically. 17px padding would give about 49.7px and clear it comfortably, but
min-height is the more honest fix -- it states the requirement rather than a value that
happens to satisfy it.

Requirements coverage:
R1 MET on its checkable terms, with a consequence in note 1. Exactly one width
  breakpoint exists in the stylesheet -- `@media (max-width: 900px)` -- and the other
  four media queries are Sprint 19's reduced-motion ones, unchanged. One route, one
  page component, no parallel component tree, no duplicated route.
R2 N/A -- removed from scope, and correctly so. /chart is genuinely untouched: git
  diff over app/chart and lib is empty. The re-scope note is the most useful thing in
  this sprint file, and it corrects a real error rather than papering over one: frames
  1 and 2 are mobile deltas on a /chart desktop design that Sprint 13 built and Sprint
  14 reverted, so there was nothing underneath to crop. Catching that before building
  against it is the difference between a re-scope and a wasted sprint.
R3 MET. The mobile written footer carries the /chart link and Copy link, and no "Cast
  again" appears at either viewport. Sprint 22's decision is inherited rather than
  reintroduced at a different width, which the sprint file specifically warned about.
R4 NOT ESTABLISHED -- see the required fix.
R5 N/A -- removed from scope. See note 4 on the stale reference left behind.
R6 MET. The 64px mask is present on the scrolling column, with both the standard and
  -webkit- properties, and the comment states why it exists rather than what it does.
R7 MET, and I re-grepped rather than inheriting it as the criterion demanded. No
  markdown library and no raw-HTML path anywhere (the only hit is display.ts's comment
  saying not to); isSafeExternalUrl still imported and used in page.tsx; package.json,
  app/layout.tsx and app/globals.css are all untouched by this diff, so fonts remain
  self-hosted; no prototype astronomy; explicit generation unchanged.
  Reduced-motion gating specifically: the mobile SVG's stars and threads use inline
  `style={{ animation: ... }}`, which cannot be wrapped in a no-preference media query
  -- but that is the identical pattern Sprint 19's desktop SVG already uses, for the
  identical reason (per-instance durations and delays), and the module carries a
  documented exception for exactly `.star`, `.thread` and `.bodyHalo` under a
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block with `animation: none !important`. Both new
  elements use those same two classes, so they are covered. I checked this rather than
  assuming it, because a new inline animation is exactly where that exception could
  have been missed.
R8 MET. I diffed the stylesheet and confirmed no rule above the breakpoint was
  removed -- every change is additive and inside `@media (max-width: 900px)`, except
  the two className additions in the components. Desktop rendering is untouched.

Verified by execution:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, unchanged -- this
  sprint adds no testable logic, which is proportionate for a stylesheet and two
  render branches.

Notes, not conditions:
1. Both constellations ship to every visitor. page.tsx now renders two complete SVGs
   -- the desktop one and a cropped mobile one -- with .desktopOnly / .mobileOnly
   toggling `display`. STAR_FIELD is 110 entries, so every page carries 220 star
   circles, two thread sets and two body sets, and a phone downloads the full desktop
   constellation including its twelve sign glyphs and ten body labels in order to never
   see it. I do not think this is avoidable as specified: viewBox cannot be changed by
   CSS, the design mandates a crop rather than a scale, and GroundTruth's own criterion
   forbids viewport-conditional server rendering. So it is the cost of the spec rather
   than a shortcut. But R1's stated rationale is that duplicated markup "doubles every
   future change and is how the two views drift apart", and that now applies to the
   constellation: a change to thread opacity has to be made twice. Worth knowing that
   the sprint bought its crop with exactly the thing R1 was written to prevent, and
   worth a comment at the top of the second SVG saying so, so the next person does not
   change one and not the other.
2. The /chart Link is duplicated too, and that one is a choice rather than a
   constraint. The comment explains it: keeping the desktop link untouched means the
   desktop diff stays exactly what Sprint 22 shipped, which serves R8. That is a
   defensible trade of R1 against R8 and it is documented, which is the part that
   matters. One link with a mobileOnly sibling would have avoided the duplication at
   the cost of touching desktop markup.
3. CopyLinkButton calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(...) with no .catch().
   The clipboard API rejects on a non-secure context or a denied permission, so on
   those paths the promise rejects unhandled, nothing is copied, the label never
   changes and nothing is logged. Production is HTTPS so the common case is fine, but
   this is the same swallow-without-a-trace pattern that became R5, R6 and R12 in
   Sprints 16 and 18. A .catch that logs, or that briefly shows "Press to copy",
   costs a line.
4. The Risks section still cites R5 -- "The truncated aspects rendered and hidden ...
   -- R5" -- after R5 was struck from Requirements in the same edit. Harmless, and the
   fourth instance of the same drift I have now flagged at Sprints 4, 15, 19 and 22: a
   requirement changes and a reference to it elsewhere in the file does not. The habit
   that fixes it is unchanged -- after amending a requirement, grep the file for its
   number before saving.
5. Small attribution slip in R3: "Sprint 19 removed the regenerate control at the
   user's direction". Sprint 22 removed it; Sprint 19 shipped it. Nothing depends on
   this, but the sprint files are the project's record of why things are the way they
   are, and this one will be read by whoever asks why there is no regenerate button.
6. Not this sprint's business, but noted for whoever is tidying: the
   devteam2/sprint-11 worktree and branch still exist, eleven sprints after that work
   landed on main.

WHAT NO GATE HERE CAN TELL ANYONE, and it is more acute in this sprint than any before
it. The sprint file says so plainly and it is right: the entire deliverable is a
layout at 390px, GroundTruth has no browser and cannot resize one, and there is no
preview environment because Sprint 5 dropped it. I can confirm one breakpoint exists,
that the guarantees survived, that desktop was not disturbed, and that the mask and
the footer structure are present. I cannot confirm the mobile layout is usable, or
that the crop frames the constellation well, or that anything is where the design puts
it. The user opening it on a phone is not a formality here -- it is the only
verification this sprint gets, and the 44px fix above is precisely the kind of thing
that is hard to judge by eye and easy to establish in the stylesheet.

Re-audit after the min-height. It is one line in one rule; keep the re-audit
proportionate to that.

CONDITIONAL: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 20, round 2. Audited at commit 69eac08. Sprint file re-read fresh.
Scope: one file, one rule, nine insertions.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. The required fix is correct in intent and incomplete in
effect, and the gap is one my own round-1 requirement created. One more line closes it.

WHAT LANDED, and it is the right instinct. min-height: 44px replaces a floor that
depended on an unmeasurable font metric with one that is true by construction and
checkable by reading the stylesheet. The commit message states exactly that reasoning.
The flex centring added alongside it is not padding of the change -- without it the
label would sit at the top of the now-taller box rather than centred, so it is
genuinely required by the min-height rather than bundled with it.

REQUIRED FIX -- min-height: 44px means 44px on the <button> and 74px on the <a>,
because nothing in this project sets box-sizing.

Four elements wear .castButton (ReadingPanel.tsx lines 115, 125, 129, 161) and they
are two different element types: a <button> for "Read the chart" / "Try again" /
"Copy link", and a next/link <a> for "Cast a new reading".

I checked what box-sizing they actually get, rather than assuming:
  - grep for box-sizing across both stylesheets: nothing.
  - grep across every emitted .css in .next/static: nothing.
  - served the built app and grepped the delivered HTML and every stylesheet it links:
    nothing.
There is no box-sizing reset anywhere in this project. So each element falls back to
its UA default, and those differ: form controls get border-box from the UA stylesheet,
anchors do not.

The mobile rule is min-height: 44px, padding: 14px, plus the 1px border inherited from
the base rule. So:
  <button>, border-box   -> min-height covers padding and border -> 44px total
  <a>,      content-box  -> 44px content box + 28px padding + 2px border -> 74px total

.mobileWrittenFooter is a flex row with no align-items, so the default stretch pulls
the Copy link button up to match. The mobile written footer therefore renders about
74px tall rather than 44px -- roughly seventy per cent over the intended height, on
the primary control of the frame this sprint exists to build.

The finding does not depend on my reading of the UA stylesheet for buttons. If buttons
were content-box too, both controls would be 74px and the row would still be wrong;
what the UA difference adds is that the two controls also disagree with each other
before flex equalises them.

Fix: add `box-sizing: border-box` to the mobile .castButton rule, beside the
min-height it makes meaningful. Then 44px means 44px for both element types, the flex
centring already added does its job, and R4 is satisfied by construction for every
element wearing the class rather than for one of the two.

I want to be clear that this is a gap my own round-1 requirement opened. Before that
fix the rule was padding-only and both element types rendered at the same intrinsic
height, whatever that height was. Asking for min-height without asking for box-sizing
is what made the two diverge. That does not make the min-height wrong -- the floor
still needs to be structural -- but the requirement was half a requirement, and I am
recording that rather than presenting this as a fresh defect found in Dev Team's work.

Round 1's coverage otherwise stands. This diff touches one rule inside the 900px
breakpoint and nothing else, so R1's single breakpoint, R7's reasserted guarantees,
R8's untouched desktop and /chart's untouched state are all unchanged from what I
verified last round. I did not re-grep them; the tree is one CSS rule different.

Verified by execution at 69eac08:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, unchanged, as expected
  for a stylesheet-only change.
- next build exits 0. The emitted rule reads min-height:44px;padding:14px;display:flex
  in the shipped CSS, so the change survives minification intact.

Notes carried from round 1, all unchanged and none blocking:
1. Both constellation SVGs still ship to every visitor -- 220 star circles per page,
   and a phone downloads the full desktop constellation to never see it. Not avoidable
   as specified, since viewBox cannot be changed by CSS and viewport-conditional
   server rendering is forbidden by GroundTruth's own criterion. Still worth a comment
   at the top of the second SVG so the next person does not change one and not the
   other.
2. The /chart Link duplication is a documented choice trading R1 against R8, not a
   constraint.
3. CopyLinkButton's clipboard promise still has no .catch(). The API rejects on a
   non-secure context or a denied permission, and on those paths nothing is copied,
   the label never changes and nothing is logged.
4. The Risks section still cites R5 after R5 was struck from Requirements.
5. R3 still attributes the regenerate removal to Sprint 19; it was Sprint 22.
6. The devteam2/sprint-11 worktree and branch still exist.

And the standing point, which this round sharpens rather than repeats: everything this
sprint delivers is invisible to every automated gate, and the two rounds of this audit
have now both turned on box-model arithmetic rather than anything a test could catch.
That is the only kind of check available here. It is not a substitute for the user
opening the page on a phone, and after this fix lands the footer height is the first
thing worth looking at, because it is the thing that has moved twice.

Re-audit after the box-sizing line. One property in one rule; keep it proportionate.

PASS: QA1 gate 1, Sprint 20, round 3. Audited at commit 9d294e8, HEAD of the main checkout,
recorded tree 2d63756e... Sprint file re-read fresh and unchanged since round 2
(f2e101d2...). Scope: one property added to one rule, plus its comment.

VERDICT: PASS.

REQUIRED FIX -- box-sizing. FIXED, and verified in the shipped output rather than in
the source.

I pulled both emitted .castButton rules out of the built stylesheet:

  desktop: {border:1px solid ...;padding:11px 18px;font-size:10.5px; ...}
  mobile:  {box-sizing:border-box;min-height:44px;padding:14px;display:flex;
            align-items:center;justify-content:center;flex:1;text-align:center}

That settles both halves of what round 2 raised. With border-box, min-height: 44px is
the border-box height, so the <button> and the next/link <a> now resolve to the same
44px rather than 44px and 74px, and the flex centring added in round 1 places the
label in the middle of it. The content box is 43.65px at IBM Plex Mono's likely
metrics, so min-height wins for both element types and the result does not depend on
the font metric at all -- which was the point of asking for min-height in the first
place.

The scoping is right too, and I checked it specifically because it is where this could
have gone wrong a third time: box-sizing appears only in the mobile rule. Desktop
keeps padding-only with no min-height and no box-sizing, and since neither element has
an explicit dimension there, content-box and border-box compute identically -- so
desktop rendering is untouched and R8 still holds. Adding box-sizing globally would
also have worked and would have been a wider change than this sprint is allowed to
make.

The comment records the reasoning, including which element type gets which UA default
and that no reset exists in this project. That is worth more than the property: the
next person to see box-sizing on one rule and not the others will otherwise assume it
is noise and tidy it away, which puts the 74px back.

Requirements coverage: R1, R3, R6, R7 and R8 stand as verified in round 1; R2 and R5
remain out of scope by the 23 Aug re-scope. R4 is now MET, by construction and for
every element wearing the class rather than for one of the two.

Verified by execution at 9d294e8:
- lint, typecheck, test: all exit 0. 179 tests across 18 files, unchanged, as expected
  for three stylesheet-only commits in a row.
- next build exits 0, and the emitted rules above are what the browser receives.
- Built with probe values for OPENAI_API_KEY and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY and grepped
  the entire .next output: both absent.

Notes, carried and unchanged. None blocking, and this is the last static gate this
sprint gets:
1. Both constellation SVGs ship to every visitor -- 220 star circles per page, and a
   phone downloads the full desktop constellation including its twelve sign glyphs and
   ten body labels to never see it. Not avoidable as specified: viewBox cannot be
   changed by CSS, and viewport-conditional server rendering is forbidden by
   GroundTruth's own criterion. Still worth a comment at the top of the second SVG, so
   the next person changing thread opacity changes both.
2. The /chart Link duplication is a documented choice trading R1 against R8.
3. CopyLinkButton's clipboard promise has no .catch(). On a non-secure context or a
   denied permission it rejects unhandled, nothing is copied, the label never changes
   and nothing is logged. Production is HTTPS so the common path is fine.
4. The Risks section still cites R5 after R5 was struck from Requirements.
5. R3 attributes the regenerate removal to Sprint 19; it was Sprint 22.
6. The devteam2/sprint-11 worktree and branch still exist, nine sprints on.

ON WHAT THESE THREE ROUNDS ACTUALLY WERE. Every one of them turned on box-model
arithmetic -- whether a line box would clear a floor, then whether min-height meant the
same thing on an anchor as on a button. No test in this repository could have caught
either, and GroundTruth cannot resize a browser it does not have. That is not a
complaint about the process; it is the shape of what a static gate can and cannot do
on a sprint whose entire deliverable is a layout. What I can now say is that the 44px
floor is structural, the guarantees survived the responsive pass, desktop was not
disturbed and /chart was not touched. What I still cannot say is whether the mobile
layout is usable, whether the crop frames the constellation well, or whether anything
sits where the design puts it.

The footer height has now moved twice under this audit -- padding-only, then min-height
without box-sizing, now min-height with it. It is the first thing to look at when the
page is opened on a device, and the sprint file is right that that step is the only
verification this sprint's actual deliverable gets.

Cleared to ship at 9d294e8.

PASS: GroundTruth live test, Sprint 20, commit 9d294e8f70ab23c7b5dbe2c0a40de702b5d64f6d. Environment: https://my-little-racoon.vercel.app and the production Supabase Data API via the anon client, 2026-08-23 ~05:20-05:25Z. VERDICT: PASS on the four criteria assigned to this gate. The mobile rendering itself -- everything this sprint exists for -- is NOT part of this verdict. The sprint file says so first and it is right. Deployed commit confirmed: /api/health/db reports {"sha":"9d294e8f70ab23c7b5dbe2c0a40de702b5d64f6d","short":"9d294e8","isLocal":false}. CRITERION 2 -- the served markup is the same for both viewports; no viewport-conditional server rendering. PASS, and this is the one criterion here a gate can settle better than a person can. Requested the same reading three ways: desktop Chrome/macOS UA iOS Safari UA (iPhone) Android Chrome UA + Sec-CH-UA-Mobile: ?1 + Viewport-Width: 390 All three responses: 214282 bytes, md5 84abd32921a23e86e12a0b4029ce4502. Byte-identical, not merely equivalent. The server does not branch on user agent or client hints, so whatever a phone gets is the same document a desktop gets and the breakpoint is doing all the work. That also means a mobile bug cannot be hiding behind UA sniffing where a desktop test would never see it. CRITERION 1 -- /reading/ serves correctly at desktop width, unchanged from Sprint 19, and /chart is unchanged from its plain form. PASS. /reading: 3 , . Raw occurrences in the served document: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0. Escaped fragments: 6. The guarantee has now survived a full visual rewrite (Sprint 19), a control removal (Sprint 22) and a responsive pass, tested by attack each time rather than carried forward on trust. Fonts and external hosts: fonts.googleapis / fonts.gstatic in the HTML -> 0. Off-origin resource-loading tags (img/script/link/iframe/source with an http(s) src) -> 0. External url() in the responsive stylesheet -> 0. CRITERION 4 -- the Sprint 14 fixture still renders a complete page. PASS. /reading/f8d046f7-... -> 200, zero framework-error markers, 4 is present. Worth stating explicitly: without it every mobile layout rule is inert, so this is the one precondition for the whole sprint that IS visible from outside, and it is satisfied. - @media (max-width:900px) ships and does what R1 describes: card goes width:100%, height:100vh, flex-direction:column; body flex-direction:column; leftColumn loses its border-right; dateBandRight display:none. - R6's mask: mask-image:linear-gradient(#000 calc(100% - 64px),#0000 100%) is present, exactly the 64px fade specified. - R4's touch target: min-height:44px is present in the shipped stylesheet, which is the "by construction, not by font metric" fix commit 69eac08 describes. TEST HYGIENE AND DATA. The escaping probe ran against the 2100-12-31 reading whose evidentiary value was spent in Sprint 18, never against a row backing this verdict, and I regenerated it afterwards through the product's own control: it now holds a real 1813-character horoscope with no probe markup in the database. No new rows created. Running count of rows this role has left in production remains ten. One OpenAI generation billed. WHAT THIS PASS DOES NOT COVER. The mobile layout. Whether the two-column grid actually collapses legibly at 900px, whether the constellation crop works, whether the condensed events grid reads, whether the fixed footer sits where it should, whether 44px targets are comfortable in the hand, whether the 64px mask fades text gracefully rather than awkwardly. I have no browser and cannot resize one, and there is no preview environment because Sprint 5 dropped previews. Everything I verified above is structural: the document is identical across viewports, the breakpoint exists, the rules are present, the guarantees hold. None of it is evidence that the phone experience is good, and this PASS must not be read as that. The sprint file assigns it to a person on a phone or in device emulation, and on a sprint whose entire deliverable is invisible to every automated gate, that step is the verification -- mine is the precondition for it.
